task_6.title: Move release provenance to PyPI attestations
task_6.description: The 2.4.0 update changes release artifact provenance distribution: GitHub releases no longer publish the `multiple.intoto.jsonl` provenance asset, because release file attestations are available through PyPI instead. No production code changes are present in the provided code diff, so this should not alter urllib3 runtime behavior or public APIs.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that release provenance expectations are updated so users no longer rely on a `multiple.intoto.jsonl` asset in GitHub releases, and instead use PyPI-hosted attestations for verifying release files.

expectation.grounded: For urllib3 2.4.0 releases, the GitHub release asset list should not include `multiple.intoto.jsonl`. Provenance or attestation data for release files since v2.3.0 should be discoverable from PyPI attestations. Because the production code diff is empty, no urllib3 import behavior, request behavior, public API, exception type, or warning behavior should change as part of this update.
expectation.conceptual: Users who verify release provenance should treat PyPI attestations as the supported source of truth, while normal library usage remains unchanged.

constraints.grounded: Do not introduce runtime behavior changes, public API changes, new warnings, or new exceptions in urllib3 solely for this release provenance change. Do not require consumers to fetch `multiple.intoto.jsonl` from GitHub releases for 2.4.0 provenance verification.
constraints.conceptual: The change should only affect how release authenticity information is obtained; it should not affect application code that depends on the library.

behavior: GitHub release assets for 2.4.0 no longer provide a `multiple.intoto.jsonl` provenance bundle.
Release file attestation lookup is expected to happen through PyPI rather than through the removed GitHub release asset.
No runtime library behavior changes are indicated by the provided production code diff.
acceptance_criteria: When a user looks for provenance for urllib3 2.4.0 release files, it should be clear that PyPI attestations are the supported location.
When a user inspects GitHub release assets for urllib3 2.4.0, they should not expect a `multiple.intoto.jsonl` asset to be present.
When existing application code imports and uses urllib3 after upgrading from 2.3.0 to 2.4.0, it should not observe behavior changes attributable to this release provenance update.
When a release verification workflow previously depended on GitHub-hosted `multiple.intoto.jsonl`, it should be updated to use PyPI attestations instead.

task_5.title: Adopt uv for development dependencies
task_5.description: The 2.4.0 update switches development dependency management to uv-backed dependency groups with a generated lock state, and aligns developer automation and documentation builds with that locked dependency workflow. This is a project maintenance and reproducibility change rather than a runtime library feature.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that project development dependency management is driven by uv-managed dependency groups and a lockfile so contributor, automation, and documentation build environments install consistent development dependencies.

expectation.grounded: Development dependency declarations formerly maintained as separate requirements-style inputs should be represented as dependency groups, with resolved development dependencies captured in a uv lock state. nox-based development sessions and documentation build setup should install dependencies through uv using the locked dependency model. Public runtime APIs, return values, warnings, and exceptions for library users should remain unchanged.
expectation.conceptual: When maintainers or build automation set up the project, development and documentation dependencies should resolve from one reproducible locked dependency model without changing how application users install, import, or use the library.

constraints.grounded: Do not introduce new runtime dependency requirements, public API changes, import-time behavior changes, or altered error, return, or warning semantics for library users. The change is limited to development dependency installation, nox session setup, and documentation build dependency setup.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade must improve reproducibility for maintainers and project infrastructure while preserving existing library behavior for end users.

behavior: Development dependency installation is expected to use uv-managed dependency groups instead of independently maintained requirements-style dependency lists.
Resolved development dependency versions are locked so local contributor environments and automation can install a consistent dependency set.
nox-based development sessions install their dependencies according to the uv-managed locked dependency configuration.
Documentation build setup installs dependencies through uv so documentation environments stay aligned with the locked dependency configuration.
No runtime behavior change is intended for library consumers, including no new public API, no changed outputs, and no changed exception or warning behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When a contributor installs development dependencies for the upgraded project, dependency resolution should come from uv dependency groups and the uv lock state rather than independent requirements-style files.
When nox sessions prepare their environments, they should install dependencies from the uv-managed locked dependency configuration.
When documentation builds prepare their environment, they should use uv for dependency installation and remain aligned with the locked dependency configuration.
When an application user installs and uses the library at runtime, behavior should remain equivalent to the previous release with respect to public APIs, return values, warnings, and exceptions.

task_3.title: Align urllib3 SSL verification flags with Python defaults
task_3.description: urllib3 2.4.0 adds a verify_flags option to create_urllib3_context() and updates its default SSL verification behavior on Python 3.13 and newer so urllib3-created contexts match Python's default SSL context for stricter certificate validation and partial-chain handling.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that urllib3-created SSL contexts expose caller-configurable certificate verification flags and, by default on Python 3.13 and newer, apply the same stricter X.509 verification policy used by Python's default SSL context.

expectation.grounded: create_urllib3_context() must accept an optional verify_flags argument. When verify_flags is omitted on Python 3.13 or newer, the returned SSLContext.verify_flags must include ssl.VERIFY_X509_PARTIAL_CHAIN and ssl.VERIFY_X509_STRICT. When an explicit verify_flags value is provided, that value must be reflected in the returned context's verify_flags, including allowing callers to pass 0 to avoid the Python 3.13 default additions. PyOpenSSL-backed contexts must expose a compatible verify_flags property whose updates affect certificate verification.
expectation.conceptual: Applications using urllib3 should get SSL verification behavior consistent with the Python runtime by default, while still being able to opt into or out of specific certificate verification flags through the public context creation API.

constraints.grounded: Existing create_urllib3_context() options for protocol selection, TLS version bounds, ciphers, certificate requirements, hostname checking, and SSL options must continue to work as before. Python versions earlier than 3.13 must not gain the new strict and partial-chain defaults unless the caller explicitly requests them through verify_flags. The PyOpenSSL compatibility layer must preserve its existing context behavior while supporting the new verify_flags surface.
constraints.conceptual: The change should align urllib3 with modern Python SSL defaults without unexpectedly tightening certificate validation for older Python runtimes or removing existing caller control over TLS configuration.

behavior: create_urllib3_context() exposes a new optional verify_flags parameter for configuring X.509 verification flags on the returned SSL context.
On Python 3.13 and newer, omitting verify_flags causes urllib3-created contexts to include partial-chain verification and strict X.509 verification by default.
On Python versions earlier than 3.13, omitting verify_flags preserves the previous default behavior and does not add the new strict or partial-chain verification flags.
Passing an explicit verify_flags value applies that caller-specified verification policy to the returned context and bypasses the Python 3.13 default additions.
PyOpenSSL-backed urllib3 contexts now provide readable and writable verify_flags support, and setting it changes the certificate store verification flags used during TLS validation.

As a result, HTTPS connections made with default urllib3 contexts on Python 3.13 and newer reject certificates that fail the stricter X.509 validation rules that Python's default SSL context enforces.
acceptance_criteria: When create_urllib3_context() is called without verify_flags on Python 3.13 or newer, the returned context should report both VERIFY_X509_PARTIAL_CHAIN and VERIFY_X509_STRICT among its verification flags.

When create_urllib3_context() is called without verify_flags on Python earlier than 3.13, the returned context should not add VERIFY_X509_PARTIAL_CHAIN or VERIFY_X509_STRICT solely because of urllib3 defaults.
When create_urllib3_context() is called with a nonzero verify_flags value, the returned context should include the caller-specified verification flag state.
When create_urllib3_context() is called with verify_flags set to 0 on Python 3.13 or newer, the returned context should not receive the new Python 3.13 strict and partial-chain defaults from urllib3.

When urllib3 is using its PyOpenSSL-backed context, reading verify_flags should return the current verification flag state and assigning verify_flags should affect certificate verification performed by that context.

When a default urllib3 SSL context is used on Python 3.13 or newer against a certificate chain that violates strict X.509 validation, the connection should fail consistently with Python's default SSL behavior.

task_2.title: Preserve urllib3 exception context when pickled
task_2.description: urllib3 2.4.0 improves serialization of exception objects so that pickling and unpickling preserve user-visible error context, especially the message and selected request or resolution details, instead of reconstructing exceptions with missing context.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that urllib3 exceptions retain their meaningful context after pickle serialization and deserialization, so callers using multiprocessing or other pickle-based transport do not receive confusing, context-free exception strings.

expectation.grounded: When urllib3 exception instances are pickled and unpickled, the restored object should remain the same exception class and should preserve the relevant public-facing context used to format the exception. PoolError and its RequestError-derived classes should preserve the original message text; RequestError-derived exceptions such as ReadTimeoutError should also preserve the request URL where applicable. MaxRetryError should preserve its URL and retry failure reason. NewConnectionError should preserve its original connection error message. NameResolutionError should preserve the host and resolution reason needed to reconstruct its displayed error context.
expectation.conceptual: Serialized urllib3 exceptions should deserialize into equivalent exceptions that still communicate what went wrong. Users should be able to inspect or print the restored exception and see the same meaningful error context they would have seen before serialization.

constraints.grounded: Do not require connection pool or connection objects themselves to be serialized for PoolError, RequestError, MaxRetryError, NewConnectionError, or NameResolutionError. Preserve existing exception class identities and existing non-pickle behavior. Avoid reducing retained context for exception types already covered by urllib3 pickle support.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should keep exception serialization lightweight and compatible while improving the information retained across process or persistence boundaries. It should not change normal exception raising behavior outside serialization.

behavior: PoolError now retains its original message through pickle round-trips, allowing the restored exception text to include the same user-facing explanation even when the pool object is not restored.
RequestError and subclasses that rely on its serialization behavior now retain both the request URL and original message through pickle round-trips.
ReadTimeoutError, as a RequestError-derived exception, no longer deserializes into an object whose string representation loses the timeout message context.
MaxRetryError now serializes its retry failure reason along with its URL, so deserialized instances can reconstruct the retry-specific error context.
NewConnectionError now retains its original connection failure message through pickle round-trips even though the connection object itself is not serialized.
NameResolutionError now retains the hostname and name resolution reason through pickle round-trips, allowing the restored exception to represent the same resolution failure context.
acceptance_criteria: Given a PoolError with a non-empty message, when it is pickled and unpickled, then the restored exception should have the same exception type and its displayed text should include the original message.

Given a RequestError-derived exception with a URL and message, when it is pickled and unpickled, then the restored exception should have the same exception type and preserve the URL and message context.

Given a ReadTimeoutError carrying timeout details, when it is pickled and unpickled, then printing or converting the restored exception to text should show the timeout details rather than missing placeholder context.
Given a MaxRetryError with a URL and failure reason, when it is pickled and unpickled, then the restored exception should keep the retry reason and continue to format as the same retry failure.

Given a NewConnectionError with a connection failure message, when it is pickled and unpickled, then the restored exception should retain that failure message even without restoring the connection object.

Given a NameResolutionError with a host and resolution reason, when it is pickled and unpickled, then the restored exception should retain the host and reason needed to communicate the same resolution failure.
When these exceptions are deserialized, they should not depend on the original connection pool or connection object being available.

task_1.title: Declare PEP 639 License Metadata
task_1.description: The 2.4.0 update applies PEP 639 license metadata so package index and dependency analysis tools can identify the project license instead of reporting it as unknown. This is a packaging metadata change and does not alter the library's runtime API or behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the distributed package advertises its license using modern Python packaging metadata so external package analysis and dependency visibility tools can correctly recognize the license.

expectation.grounded: The project metadata for version 2.4.0 should include explicit PEP 639 license fields in the package configuration. Consumers inspecting package metadata through Python packaging tools, package indexes, or dependency scanners should observe a declared license rather than an unknown license. No public urllib3 runtime APIs, return values, warnings, or exceptions are changed by this update.
expectation.conceptual: Users and compliance tools should be able to determine the package license from the published package metadata without relying on inference, while existing application behavior remains unchanged.

constraints.grounded: The change must be limited to packaging/license metadata semantics and must not change urllib3's public runtime behavior, import behavior, networking behavior, supported APIs, emitted warnings, or exception behavior.
constraints.conceptual: Improve license discoverability for distribution and compliance workflows without introducing any application-facing behavior change.

behavior: Published package metadata now explicitly declares the project license according to PEP 639.
Package metadata consumers should no longer need to treat the package license as unknown when reading the declared metadata.
Runtime behavior is unchanged: importing and using the library should expose the same user-facing APIs and operational semantics as before this metadata update.
acceptance_criteria: When a user or dependency analysis tool inspects the package metadata for version 2.4.0, it should find an explicit license declaration compatible with PEP 639.

When a package index or dependency visibility service reads the published metadata, it should be able to present the package license instead of reporting it as unknown due to missing license metadata.
When existing applications upgrade from 2.3.0 to 2.4.0, their runtime usage of urllib3 should continue to behave the same because the change is metadata-only.

task_4.title: Fix Emscripten partial streaming reads
task_4.description: Fix Emscripten streaming response handling so partial low-level reads are treated as valid intermediate chunks instead of premature end-of-stream signals. This prevents chunked consumers from missing data when JavaScript supplies arbitrary-sized chunks.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Emscripten streaming HTTP responses can be consumed in repeated partial reads without prematurely closing the response before all available data has been read.

expectation.grounded: For urllib3's Emscripten HTTP response wrapper, calling read(amt) with a positive amount must return the bytes supplied by the underlying stream and update length_remaining when known, but a non-empty result shorter than amt must not by itself close the response body. The response body should close only when an empty read is observed or when the response has a certain content length and length_remaining reaches zero.
expectation.conceptual: Streaming reads should continue across arbitrary transport chunk boundaries. A short chunk is valid data, not proof that the response is complete, unless the stream is empty or the known response length has been fully consumed.

constraints.grounded: Preserve existing behavior for full-body reads, response body caching when enabled, length_remaining accounting, and closing once a certain-length response is fully consumed. Do not change non-Emscripten response behavior or treat partial non-empty chunks as terminal.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should only make streaming more reliable; it must not alter normal response consumption, cached full reads, or completion detection for responses whose total length is known.

behavior: Bounded Emscripten response reads may return fewer bytes than requested without closing the underlying response body.
A bounded read that returns non-empty data keeps the stream open when the remaining response length is unknown or not yet exhausted.
length_remaining continues to be reduced by the number of bytes returned when the response length is tracked.
The response body closes after an empty read.
The response body closes when the response length is certain and length_remaining reaches zero.
Unbounded reads still read all currently available data, cache the body when requested, update length_remaining, and close on empty data or confirmed completion.
acceptance_criteria: Given an Emscripten streaming response whose underlying source returns a non-empty chunk smaller than the requested read amount, when read(amt) is called, it should return that chunk and leave the response open for subsequent reads.

Given an Emscripten streaming response with more data available after a short chunk, when a consumer repeatedly calls read(amt), it should be able to accumulate the complete response instead of stopping at the first short chunk.
Given a response with a certain content length, when reads consume the final byte and length_remaining reaches zero, the response body should close.
Given any Emscripten response read that returns no bytes, when completion is evaluated, the response body should close.
When full-body reads are used with content caching enabled, the response body data should still be cached and completion should still be detected normally.
